summary.headline: ESAF SFB Q2 FY27 PAT doubled QoQ to Rs 160 crore; gross NPA fell to 2.8% from 8.5% YoY, and FY27 ROA guidance is now 2%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed sharp improvement in profitability and asset quality, with PAT of Rs 160 crore (up from Rs 80 crore QoQ), ROA of 1.5% and ROE of 26.5% annualised. Total business grew 25% YoY to Rs 52,400 crore, while QoQ loan growth slowed to about 3% as management attributed the moderation to StratoNeXt migration. Slippages fell to Rs 87 crore from Rs 342 crore a year earlier, and management called the Rs 626 crore technical write-off probably the last of the legacy NPA. StratoNeXt (core banking on Oracle FLEXCUBE) went live on October 26, 2026, and management expects opex to rise, taking cost-to-income to around 60% for the year.

segments.name: MARG (MSME, Agri, Retail, Gold)
segments.commentary: Rs 13,938 crore, +38% YoY, 58% of gross advances. Gold loans Rs 10,456 crore with GNPA 0.1%; Agri +66%, Gold +39%, Mortgage +39%, Retail +34% YoY.

segments.name: Emerging Households (EH)
segments.commentary: Grew 134% YoY and 5% QoQ to 32% of gross advances; Individual and Enterprise segments growing fastest, FIG stable.

segments.name: Microfinance (group loans)
segments.commentary: Declined 65% YoY as borrowers are migrated to individual and secured products; unsecured book (incl. MFI) grew 15% YoY to Rs 8,557 crore.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits Rs 28,466 crore (+24% YoY), retail deposits Rs 25,475 crore (89% of total, +15% YoY); CASA Rs 6,645 crore (+10% YoY), CASA ratio 23.3%; NRI deposits +17% YoY.

guidance_outlook: ROA guidance changed to 2% for full FY27 (earlier guidance was quarterly ROA of 2% by year end); FY28 guidance to be given next quarter.
Cost-to-income to be around 60% for FY27 given StratoNeXt capitalisation and branch build-up; current level 58%.
Credit cost expected around 2% for FY27; around 1.5% considered a reasonable guess for FY28.
Funding cost expected to rise marginally in Q3; NIM of 8.2% seen as absorbing this, but further policy rate hikes could pressure NIMs.
PPOP expected to remain stable in H2; management expects the earlier ~20% growth trajectory to resume by FY28.
Gross slippage ratio of about 1.6% (annualised) expected to continue for the rest of FY27.
capex_capacity: StratoNeXt (ESAF 2.0) went live on October 26, 2026, migrating to Oracle FLEXCUBE core banking with upgraded applications and infrastructure; management is now focused on stabilisation.
Network at 831 banking outlets (10 added in the quarter), 722 ATMs, 1,060 customer service centres and 31 institutional business correspondents across 24 states and 2 UTs.
Capitalisation of StratoNeXt spend will begin now, adding opex for the next half; total spend amount not disclosed and will be provided later.
Bank has decided to infuse about Rs 1,000 crore of capital; valuation not yet decided; no urgent need given CAR of 24.1%; strategic capital infusion being explored.
demand_pricing: Total business Rs 52,400 crore (+25% YoY); Rs 53,450 crore including IBPC transactions.
Gross advances Rs 23,934 crore (+25% YoY); secured Rs 15,377 crore (+32% YoY per CFO; +35% per ED), 64% of advances; unsecured Rs 8,557 crore (+15% YoY).
Management said QoQ loan growth moderated to about 3% due to migration focus; analyst noted this.

Gold SMA-0 about Rs 1,080-1,085 crore (about Rs 990 crore gold) and SMA-1 about Rs 250 crore (about Rs 200 crore gold), attributed to gold price volatility in September and early October; price now stabilising.
Gold book average LTV around 76% (current basis), mostly bullet repayment, no top-up loans.
Maharashtra and Karnataka (about 15-16% of portfolio) performing well, but drought may affect collections if prolonged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow about 10% QoQ when loans grew about 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to asset mix and to NPAs last year on which interest could not be recognised; resolving NPAs restored full income recognition. Technical write-off had no income reversal component.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Bank achieve about 20% growth in FY28, and what about insurance income?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said FY28 growth should return to the earlier trajectory. Insurance income was Rs 25 crore in Q2 and Rs 124 crore in FY26; the IRDA draft guideline impact is still being assessed.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a capital raise and at what valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank has decided to infuse about Rs 1,000 crore but has not decided valuation; CAR is 24% so no urgent need, though strategic infusion is being explored and a raise this year is not ruled out.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on ROA and credit cost for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ROA guidance is now 2% for the full year; FY28 guidance next quarter. Credit cost about 2% for FY27 and around 1.5% hoped for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure in drought-hit states and gold SMA, and what restructuring is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra and Karnataka collections are holding up but prolonged drought could hit them. Restructuring is permitted but not expected to be material; gold loans are not eligible for crop-loan forbearance.

qa_highlights.question: How much of MARG and EH is migrated from MFI borrowers, and what was the Q2 other income from one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a small share of MARG/EH customers came from MFI graduates; most are new to the bank. Q2 other income included Rs 64 crore from PSLC sales and other non-recurring items.

risks_watch: StratoNeXt post-go-live stability: transaction accuracy, system performance and any operational disruption, plus opex rising toward 60% cost-to-income.
Gold loan SMA-0/SMA-1 (about Rs 1,085 crore SMA-0, mostly gold) could roll into NPAs if gold prices stay volatile.
Drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka (about 15-16% of portfolio) could hit collections if it persists through the year.
Funding cost rising in Q3 and any further RBI rate hikes could compress the 8.2% NIM.
Insurance commission (Rs 124 crore in FY26) may be reduced by IRDA's revised guidelines.
Kerala deposit concentration remains high; the Bank plans to diversify over time. CASA ratio of 23.3% and its year-end target remain a watch item.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, profitability and the StratoNeXt milestone, with explicit caution on gold-price volatility, drought, RBI tightening and geopolitical risks. Evasive on FY28 ROA and capital-raise valuation, deferring both to later updates.
key_quotes: The successful implementation has strengthened our technology backbone and established a more scalable and resilient platform for the Bank's future growth.
Our gross slippage ratio for Q2 FY27 on an annualized basis stands reduced to 1.6% and is expected to have the same trend in the remaining fiscal year.
We remain cautious and watchful for the increased volatility in global energy prices and the persisting El Nino conditions.
Our advantage is that, still we have got only 76% LTV and we are very conservative in fixing per gram gold rate for the purpose of lending.
